name: CapCut
tagline: Consumer video editor with templates, captions, effects, and AI tools

pricing.notes: Official resource checked 2026-07-30 lists Pro at $19.99/month and $179.99/year; pricing can vary by region/app store.

verdictSummary: A captioner/trimmer/exporter is buildable, but CapCut's value is mobile editing polish, effects/templates, asset library, TikTok workflow, and real-time rendering.
coreLoopDIY: Upload video, auto-caption, cut/trim, add simple templates/effects, and export social aspect ratios.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because short-form editing is fast on a phone and full of reusable trends/effects.

priorArt.name: Shotcut
priorArt.desc: Open-source video editor; powerful prior art but not mobile/template-first like CapCut.

alternatives.name: Adobe Express
alternatives.desc: Browser editing, captions, graphics and templates without a watermark; premium stock and clever tricks still wave from behind glass.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install the Adobe Express desktop/mobile app.
facts.engines: Adobe Firefly models power the generative features.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, uploads, libraries and brand assets live in Adobe's cloud; exports include image, PDF and video files.
facts.gapVsPaid: Adobe Express has a shallower timeline, fewer trend-driven effects and templates, and fewer advanced mobile-video tools than CapCut.

alternatives.name: Clipchamp
alternatives.desc: CapCut’s less chaotic browser cousin; free exports stop at 1080p, not at a watermark.

facts.install: Use the browser editor or the bundled Windows app after signing in with a Microsoft account.
facts.engines: Microsoft-hosted AI services provide captions, voiceovers and silence removal; exact model names are not published.
facts.dataFormat: Original media stays local by default; project metadata is cloud-synced, optional content backup uploads media, and exports are MP4 or audio files.
facts.gapVsPaid: Clipchamp Free tops out at 1080p and has a smaller effects, template and mobile-creation ecosystem than CapCut.

alternatives.name: DaVinci Resolve
alternatives.desc: A film studio hiding behind a free download; the cleverest AI toys stay in Studio.

facts.install: Download the macOS, Windows or Linux installer after completing Blackmagic Design's registration form.
facts.engines: The DaVinci Neural Engine powers AI-assisted features; many of the most advanced tools are reserved for Resolve Studio.
facts.dataFormat: Project libraries/databases and referenced media live locally by default; Blackmagic Cloud project libraries are optional.
facts.gapVsPaid: Resolve has a steep professional learning curve and lacks CapCut's instant social templates and trend-driven mobile workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: The download requires registration, and useful performance generally needs a capable GPU and substantial disk space.

alternatives.name: Kdenlive
alternatives.desc: A real multitrack editor with local captions, minus the template casino.

facts.install: Install the official Windows, macOS or Linux package.
facts.engines: Speech-to-text can run local VOSK or OpenAI Whisper models.
facts.dataFormat: .kdenlive project files are MLT/XML references to local media; proxies, thumbnails and backups live in project folders.
facts.gapVsPaid: Kdenlive lacks CapCut's large template/effect ecosystem, mobile workflow and one-click consumer AI tools.
facts.setupBlocker: Core editing installs cleanly; local captioning requires downloading and configuring a speech model.

alternatives.name: Shotcut
alternatives.desc: A sturdy desktop editor that would rather give you controls than trends.

facts.install: Install an official Windows, macOS or Linux build; portable builds are also offered.
facts.engines: Speech-to-text runs local Whisper through whisper.cpp with downloadable GGML models.
facts.dataFormat: .mlt project files are MLT XML references to local media, with rendered files written wherever the user chooses.
facts.gapVsPaid: Shotcut provides editing controls rather than CapCut's trend templates, polished mobile workflow and automated social effects.
facts.setupBlocker: Core editing installs cleanly; speech-to-text requires downloading a compatible Whisper model.

rejectedAlternatives.name: OpenCut
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The famous answer is between codebases: classic is archived and the replacement is still a rewrite.

notes: Good category because 'AI captions' are trivial, but editor/template depth is not.
prompt:
Build me a video captioning and clipping tool to replace CapCut Pro.
Requirements:

- A CLI: Python + ffmpeg + faster-whisper. clip input.mp4 transcribes and
  burns captions; --cut 0:12-0:58 trims first; a folder as input batches
  every video in it.
- Captions from word-level timestamps, grouped 3-5 words per line, rendered
  as ASS subtitles: bold font, white fill, black outline, centered in the
  lower third, burned in with ffmpeg.
- style.json controls the look in one place: font, size, colors, margin.
- Aspect exports: --format 9x16 (blur-pad or center-crop, chosen by flag),
  1x1, and 16x9, with bitrate defaults sane for phone playback.
- --srt writes the plain subtitle file next to the video so I can fix
  typos, then --from-srt re-burns without re-transcribing.
- Output is <name>-<format>.mp4 beside the input; never overwrite a source
  file.
- Fully local and offline after the model download: no accounts, no uploads,
  no telemetry. Use the GPU when present, CPU still works.
- Out of scope: a timeline editor, effects and templates, and a music
  library; CapCut's editor polish is the product. This is for talking-head
  clips.
- README: installing ffmpeg and choosing a whisper model size.
